items.title: Indian stocks set for pullback after sharp rally on oil slide, foreign inflows
items.description: Indian markets are likely to experience a decline on Friday following a global market selloff. Investor concerns are rising due to the impact of the US Democratic win on regulations and foreign policy. Both Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex ended their six-session winning streak on Thursday. Foreign institutional investors made substantial stock purchases amid shifting market dynamics related to AI.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 large-cap stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the NSE large-cap pack, eight stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 5, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Microfinance lenders tread cautiously amid rural stress
items.description: The microfinance sector experienced varied performance in the second quarter of FY27, reflecting economic uncertainty. Bandhan Bank and CreditAccess Grameen saw declines in their microfinance portfolios, while IndusInd Bank grew its portfolio. Lenders are concerned about the impact of drought and inflation on rural borrowers. Estimates for the sector's growth varied between credit information companies, indicating inconsistencies. Collection discipline has improved, but localized climate disruptions continue to pose risks.

items.title: Sensex stages biggest rally since April as FIIs turn aggressive buyers
items.description: Foreign institutional investors significantly increased their purchases of Indian stocks, leading to substantial market gains. The BSE Sensex rose by 2,008.61 points, achieving its biggest jump since April. Easing crude oil prices contributed to reduced inflation expectations and improved India's macroeconomic outlook. Positive global cues, including gains in US markets, further supported investor sentiment and market performance.

items.title: Sebi eases accreditation norms for AIF, SIF and PMS investors
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new regulation allowing alternative investment fund managers to handle investor accreditation. This initiative is designed to streamline the accreditation process for investors looking for investment options. Managers are now authorized to evaluate eligibility during onboarding or at any stage of the scheme, providing greater flexibility.

items.title: Sebi relaxes cash market settlement rules for mutual funds
items.description: Securities and Exchange Board of India has permitted mutual fund schemes to net fund obligations. This new regulation is set to come into effect starting April 1, 2027. It allows net settlement of funds at the individual scheme level while maintaining gross settlement for securities. Fund obligations cannot be adjusted across different schemes, and inter-scheme funding remains prohibited. Proceeds from outright sales must be funded separately for non-outright obligations.

items.title: FIIs turn buyers in IT, telecom stocks in second half of October ahead of Diwali
items.description: Technology stocks in India are seeing increased interest from foreign institutional investors as Diwali approaches. After struggling in the first half of October, the IT and telecom sectors have gained attention. Foreign portfolio investors made significant net purchases of Indian equities in late October. This upward trend follows substantial selling earlier in the month. The shift highlights a renewed focus on technology investments within the Indian market.

items.title: D-Street braces for gap-down opening on negative GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: On Thursday, the Nifty index exceeded 24,000 for the first time in nearly two months. This rise was supported by falling crude oil prices and substantial foreign institutional investments. Analysts expect Indian equities to maintain a positive trend as the festive season approaches. The rupee also appreciated slightly against the US dollar due to robust foreign fund inflows. Overall, the market outlook remains optimistic despite fluctuating conditions.

items.title: Stocks in news: Bharti Airtel, LIC, Titan, ONGC, Bharti Hexacom, Glenmark Pharma and Astral
items.description: Indian equity markets continued their upward trend, highlighted by the Nifty 50 gaining 576 points. Bharti Airtel, LIC, and Titan Company reported strong profit increases for the September quarter. ONGC also posted a substantial rise in consolidated profit compared to last year. In contrast, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals faced a significant decline in net profit this quarter. Overall, corporate developments are influencing investor sentiment as markets react to earnings reports.

items.title: M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
items.description: The BSE has hit a significant milestone as the collective market capitalization of listed firms exceeded ₹500 lakh crore, driven by a comprehensive market rally and new listings. Although many indices remain below their historical peaks, strong demand from foreign portfolio investors and favorable global signals have led to an uplift in market sentiment. Challenges such as geopolitical shifts and profit booking, however, could threaten future expansion.

items.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
items.description: In October 2026, new demat account additions reached a nine-month high, driven by strong IPO activity. NSDL and CDSL reported adding nearly 3.36 million accounts during the month. The total number of demat accounts at the end of October was approximately 244 million. The increase in account openings was mainly influenced by the successful launch of several public issues.

items.title: Stock Radar: Coforge stock hits fresh record high in November 2026; will the rally continue?
items.description: Coforge Ltd has successfully broken out of a lengthy consolidation phase that lasted over two months. The stock now shows potential targets above the 2,200 levels in the upcoming weeks. Key support levels are established, with immediate support at 1,940 and previous resistance around 2,000. Experts suggest maintaining strategic stop losses to manage potential downside risks effectively. Momentum indicators favor continued bullish trends, indicating further growth opportunities for traders.

items.title: Gold loan NPA rises in first five months while eases over a three-year horizon
items.description: India’s gold loan market has experienced a rise in non-performing assets, reaching 0.78% by August 2023. The total outstanding volume grew nearly threefold to Rs 22.5 lakh crore recently. Borrowers are increasingly taking multiple loans, with many having four or more gold loans. The market also saw 5.5 crore active borrowers, indicating its broad consumer reach.
